transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—thanks for coming today. What brings you in to see me?

Well, I came in because... I don't know, ever since my sister and her new baby moved back into the house, I've just been a lot more on edge. And down, I guess. I find myself snapping over really little stuff at home. And then by the time I get to my classes or show up at the shop for work, I'm already completely drained. I'm still getting by, mostly, but I've missed a couple of deadlines for school. I even had to back out of helping build the set for the theater department because I just couldn't keep everything straight in my head anymore.
About how long ago did your sister and her baby move in, and did your mood and anxiety symptoms start around that same time?

Um, I was doing okay before my sister and the baby moved in. But yeah, to answer your question, the trouble started within a couple of weeks of the house getting so crowded. It really didn't take long for it to hit me.
Besides feeling on edge and irritable, have you also been feeling persistently sad, hopeless, or have you lost interest in things you used to enjoy?

I wouldn't say hopeless, no. Or constantly sad. I mean, I feel a little down sometimes just because it's so chaotic at the house, but it's not like this deep, dark sadness. 

And I haven't really lost interest in my usual stuff. Like, with the theater set... I still wanted to help build it. I just honestly didn't have the energy or the focus to actually get it done. It's more that I'm just completely drained and stressed out, not that I don't care about things anymore.
Have you been feeling especially nervous, worried, or on edge much of the time, with things like a racing heart, muscle tension, or trouble relaxing?

I mean, I'm definitely stressed and on edge, like I mentioned earlier. But I wouldn't say I'm constantly worried about things. And I haven't noticed my heart racing or getting tense muscles or anything physical like that. 

It is hard to relax at home, yeah, but that's mostly just because it's so loud and crowded now with my sister and the baby. It's not like my body is panicking or anything, if that makes sense. I'm just really drained by it all.
Besides snapping at people, have you noticed yourself acting out in other ways lately—like being more argumentative, breaking rules, or doing things impulsively that aren't like you?

No, not really. I mean, I'm not breaking rules or doing anything reckless or impulsive. It's really just the snapping when I get overwhelmed by all the noise. I haven't been getting into big arguments or doing things that are out of character, other than just having a shorter fuse than normal right now.
Aside from feeling stressed and on edge, have you noticed yourself feeling low, tearful, or down on yourself at all during this time, even briefly?

No, not really. I mean, I'm not crying or feeling really down on myself or anything like that. It's really just the stress and feeling overwhelmed by everything going on at home. I don't feel low in that way.
How much is this stress affecting your daily functioning—like, are you still managing to attend classes and work most days, or has it really disrupted your ability to keep up with things?

I'm still managing to go to class and work most days. I haven't missed any shifts or anything like that. But, um, I have turned in a couple of assignments late recently. And I actually had to drop out of helping build the set for this community theater project I was doing. I just couldn't keep up with everything on top of how drained I've been feeling. So I'm still functioning, mostly, but things are definitely slipping a little bit.
It's been a few weeks since your sister and the baby moved in—has this been going on continuously since then, or has it been more on-and-off?

Yeah, it's been pretty continuous. I'd say it's been going on for about a month now, basically right since my sister and her baby moved back into the house. It hasn't really been on-and-off, just kind of a constant thing every day since they got here.
